statements.venue: Press release on introduction of the FRONTIER Act
statements.quote: The FRONTIER Act is a targeted bill with clear, uniform transparency, and safety standards, instead of a fifty-state patchwork. I'm glad to support this bipartisan effort so that Congress acts before this technology outruns us.
statements.context: Peters was one of the members introducing the FRONTIER Act, a bill setting transparency, audit and catastrophic-risk reporting rules for the largest frontier AI developers.
statements.reason: He supports safety standards and says Congress must act before the technology outruns it, but names no catastrophic or serious danger from AI itself; the bill text concerns catastrophic risk but his own words do not.

record: Introduced the FRONTIER Act alongside lead sponsors Obernolte and Trahan: tiered transparency, independent audits, incident reporting and a uniform national standard for reporting catastrophic risk from the most advanced AI models.
grade_reason: His only AI statement found (July 2026, backing the FRONTIER Act) supports AI safety standards but does not itself acknowledge catastrophic risk.
notes: 8 web searches ran, none refused. Many results were about Sen. Gary Peters (Michigan), not this representative; those were excluded. The Obernolte release lists Peters among members who introduced the FRONTIER Act 'alongside' the lead sponsors; formal co-sponsor status on congress.gov was not checked. A reviewer could argue for C because the bill he co-introduced targets catastrophic risk, but his own words only say Congress should act 'before this technology outruns us'. No source showed him co-sponsoring the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (search results on its House co-sponsors conflict and do not name him). Search results also mention his co-backing of the Great American AI Act discussion draft and a bill to stop data center construction at NAVWAR (data center, not catastrophic risk); not opened. The first page of his own press releases (scottpeters.house.gov/press-releases) had no AI items; his op-eds page had no AI titles. Left out per House instructions: any many-signer August/September 2026 House letters.
